scorecards.analysisText:
PHASE 0A — ROUTING COMPLETE

Year anchor — five row label mappings (mandatory, written before any table):

  • Sharescope "current H1/H2" → FY25 partial actuals (H1 = six months ended 31 Mar 2025; H2 = six months ended 30 Sep 2025)
  • Sharescope "1y ago" → FY24 actuals (year ended 30 Sep 2024)
  • Sharescope "2y ago" → FY23 actuals (year ended 30 Sep 2023)
  • Sharescope "3y ago" → FY22 actuals (year ended 30 Sep 2022)
  • Sharescope "FY1 fc" → FY26 consensus forecast (year ending 30 Sep 2026)
  • Sharescope "FY2 fc" → FY27 consensus forecast (year ending 30 Sep 2027)

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

The FY25 results RNS explicitly states: "The year-on-year FX effects were minimal: on the average FY25 USD to GBP exchange rate of 1.30 vs average FY24 USD to GBP exchange rate of 1.27 the revenues decreased by less than 1% for the Group."

Constant currency is not explicitly disclosed as within 0.5pp of reported, but the disclosed FX impact is stated as less than 1% on revenues — confirming near-nil impact. North America was ~28% of FY25 revenue (£12.5m/£44.8m). USD exposure is the primary non-GBP currency but the company itself quantifies the impact as sub-1%. No Phase 0B penalty or badge applied — FX impact disclosed as immaterial by management. Reporting currency: GBP throughout.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

OMG · Q4 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 30/09/25

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = Q4). Interpreting RNS as FY25 full year results. Market now expects H1 FY26 results or H1 guidance. Next year end 30/9/26 = FY26.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 2.6p · Revenue £49.1m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 2.9p · Revenue £53.3m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot period (18 May 2025 → 2 Apr 2026): 2.7p → 2.6p, net change −0.1p (−3.7%). One downgrade step in late Feb 2026 (2.7p → 2.6p). Revenue moved 46.6m → 49.1m over same period — a material upward revision to revenue consensus (+5.4%), anchored around the Dec 2025 step-change (46.2m → 49.1m). Last-4-week EPS trend: 🟡 FLAT (2.6p throughout). Revenue flat at £49.1m for 4 weeks. Mixed picture: revenue upgraded significantly, EPS ticked down slightly.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg — Revenue): 3yr avg H1% of FY = 49.4%. FY26e consensus £49.1m × 49.4% = £24.3m H1 revenue baseline. 3yr avg H1% of FY for EPS = 52.5% (Sharescope-supplied). FY26e EPS 2.6p × 52.5% = 1.37p H1 EPS baseline.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £20.1m · Adjusted basic EPS 0.12p (from RNS note 4; statutory basic EPS −0.63p from continuing operations)

    Note on EPS baseline: FY25 H1 adjusted basic EPS was 0.12p. The Sharescope "current H1" EPS of 0.1p is consistent with this. The company uses adjusted EBIT as primary metric but Sharescope tracks adjusted basic EPS. Used 0.12p as H1 FY25 actual throughout.

  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-H1 mode — comparing implied FY26 H2 vs avg of last 3 historical H2s):
    • Revenue: FY26e £49.1m − H1 FY25 actual £20.1m = implied H2 £29.0m. Historical H2 actuals: FY24 H2 £17.9m, FY25 H2 £24.7m, FY23 H2 £23.0m (2y ago). Avg of last 3 = £21.9m. Implied H2 vs avg: +£7.1m, +32% above avg — flagged for Phase 3.3.
    • EPS: FY26e 2.6p − H1 FY25 0.12p = implied H2 2.48p. Historical H2 actuals: FY24 H2 0.4p (Sharescope 1y ago), FY25 H2 1.4p (current H2), FY23 H2 2.4p (2y ago). Avg of last 3 = 1.43p. Implied H2 vs avg: +1.05p, +73% above avg — significant flag.
  • FX: Immaterial — management-disclosed sub-1% revenue impact; no penalty applied.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP. Net cash (negative net borrowing): FY22 H2 −£7.2m / FY23 H2 −£9.9m / FY24 H2 −£10.6m / FY25 H2 −£0.9m → wait — cross-check required: RNS states FY25 net cash £37.3m (cash + FTDs). Sharescope "current H2" net borrowing = −£0.9m appears to be using a different net debt definition (likely excluding fixed-term deposits). Will use RNS-disclosed £37.3m as the authoritative balance sheet figure per workflow discipline. FY26e fc net borrowing Sharescope: −£33.7m / FY27e: −£34.6m (likely also including/excluding FTDs on same basis as current). ND/EBITDA: all negative (net cash throughout). Interest cover: negative (net cash position — finance income exceeds finance expense). Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — balance sheet not a constraint on estimates.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

OMG · Q4 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 30/09/25

RNS type: Full Year Results (audited preliminary results, FY ended 30 September 2025, released December 2025)

1. Revenue figures

FY25 Group revenue: £44.8m, up +8% vs FY24 £41.5m. vs FY26e consensus at time of results (Sharescope snapshot shows consensus moved to £49.1m in Dec 2025 — the step-change from £44.8m → £49.1m appears to reflect the post-results upgrade to include FY26 extended year to 31 Dec 2026, see accounting reference date change note below). FY25 actual vs the pre-results FY25 consensus: snapshot at 01 Nov 2025 shows £44.8m — exactly in line. The Oct 2025 trading update guided "broadly in line with market expectations" with stated consensus £46.2m. FY25 actual £44.8m is £1.4m (−3%) below the stated Oct 2025 consensus of £46.2m — a modest revenue miss vs that pre-announced benchmark. However this is flagged as the market had already reset to £44.8m in the Sharescope series by Nov 2025 snapshots, suggesting broker models had already moved.

"overall Group revenue is expected to be broadly in line with market expectations. The Group considers FY25 market consensus at the date of this announcement to be: Revenue £46.2m" (Oct 2025 trading update)

"Revenue £44.8m (FY24: £41.5m), up 8% on prior year" (FY25 preliminary results)

⚠️ Important structural note — accounting reference date change: The company announced on 16 December 2025 a change to 31 December accounting reference date. FY26 will be a 15-month period ending 31 December 2026. The Sharescope £49.1m FY1 fc almost certainly reflects this extended 15-month year. This is a critical distortion for all consensus comparisons — 15 months vs 12 months is not a like-for-like comparison. Flagged as a major structural issue for Phase 3 and Phase 4.

Motion Capture revenue: £32.0m (FY24: £38.6m), −17% YoY. Smart Manufacturing revenue: £12.8m (FY24: £2.9m), +341% YoY (includes Sempre and Amber Optix acquisitions; organic growth +38%).

"Motion Capture revenue was £32.0m (FY24: £38.6m), reflecting continued US academic and entertainment headwinds and post-COVID normalisation of opening order book to £1.0m (FY24: £11.5m)"

2. EPS / earnings figures

FY25 adjusted basic EPS: 1.55p (FY24 restated: 3.01p), −49% YoY. Statutory basic EPS: −0.55p (FY24: +0.58p).

FY25 adjusted EBIT: £2.2m (FY24: £1.7m), +29% YoY. PBT: £0.1m (FY24: £0.5m restated). Finance income fell significantly to £1.3m (FY24: £2.3m) due to lower cash balances post buybacks and acquisitions — this is the dominant driver of the EPS decline vs FY24.

vs FY26e consensus: Sharescope FY1 fc EPS = 2.6p. However this is for a 15-month FY26 — not comparable to the 1.55p FY25 (12-month). On a run-rate basis, FY25 annualised adjusted basic EPS of 1.55p suggests FY26 12-month equivalent would need significant EBIT growth to reach 2.6p even on a pro-rata 15/12 basis. This is the key tension.

"Adjusted Basic EPS 1.55p (FY24: 3.01p), −49%"

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate FY25: tax charge £766k on PBT of £85k — statutory rate wildly elevated by deferred tax movements. On adjusted PBT basis: adjusted PBT £2.7m (per note 6: adjusted EBIT £2.2m + finance income net £0.5m). Tax on adjusted basis: £766k charge / £2.7m adjusted PBT = effective rate ~28%. Normalised UK rate 25%. Deviation of ~3pp — at threshold. Restated adjusted EPS at 25%: adjusted PAT would be £2.7m × 75% = £2.025m / 124.4m shares = 1.63p vs reported 1.55p. Gap is modest (0.08p). No material EPS quality distortion — no 🚨 flag required, within normal range.

FY26e EPS bridge (construct here):

  • (1) New base EPS: FY25 adjusted basic EPS = 1.55p (12-month year, 124.4m weighted avg shares)
  • (2) 15-month year adjustment: FY26 is 15 months. Pro-rata uplift on 12-month run rate = ×15/12 = ×1.25. Mechanically, 1.55p × 1.25 = 1.94p purely from the extra quarter — before any growth.
  • (3) Inorganic annualisation delta: Sempre acquired Oct 2024 (contributed full H1 FY25 + full H2 FY25 = full FY25). Amber Optix acquired Apr 2025, small (£0.6m revenues). No major incomplete-year inorganic items — both fully annualised in FY25 base. Delta: +0.0p (fully baked in).
  • (4) Organic EBITDA growth delta: Smart Manufacturing organic growth guided as strong; Motion Capture facing US headwinds but APAC/EMEAI improving. FY26 EBITDA consensus £7.3m vs FY25 EBITDA (implied from RNS: adjusted EBIT £2.2m + D&A £4.7m = ~£6.9m). Implied EBITDA growth £0.4m. On 124m shares this is ~0.3p. However this is for 12 months — on 15-month basis add ~25% further = ~0.4p.
  • (5) Interest step-up: Net cash position, finance income declining (£1.7m received vs £1.3m income). Interest income will continue declining as cash depletes. Negative delta vs FY25 finance income: estimated −£0.3m vs FY25, −0.2p impact.
  • (6) Share buyback benefit: £8.3m spent buying 15.9m shares in FY25 at avg 52p. Share count reduced from ~131m to ~115m by end FY25, further reduction ongoing (£10m programme ~£8.6m deployed by Dec 2025 per RNS). Diluted count FY26 likely ~112m vs FY25 weighted avg 124.4m. This is a meaningful per-share tailwind: same PAT on fewer shares. Delta: ~+0.15p.

Implied FY26e EPS (15-month): 1.94p (base × 15/12) + 0.3p (EBITDA growth) − 0.2p (interest drag) + 0.15p (buyback) = ~2.2p. Sharescope FY1 fc is 2.6p. Gap of ~0.4p — suggests consensus may be pencilling in more EBIT growth or the interest drag is smaller than estimated. The 2.6p consensus could be achievable if Smart Manufacturing delivers a further step-change in EBIT. Revision direction: consensus broadly achievable but not obviously beatable on current trajectory. Referenced in Phase 4 — not restated there.

3. Order book / forward work

Motion Capture in-year order intake FY25: £34.8m, up +21% vs FY24 £28.8m. Opening FY26 order book: £1.0m (FY25 opening: £11.5m — now normalised post-COVID unwind).

"in-year order intake up 21% to £34.8m (FY24: £28.8m), demonstrating positive underlying demand"

Smart Manufacturing: good H2 visibility cited in interim results; "building orderbook and pipeline which continues beyond the current financial year" — qualitative only, no quantum stated for FY26.

AGM (25 Feb 2026) trading update: Vicon secured two large Entertainment orders totalling £2.7m from Eastern Europe and Japan, further China stage extensions, two Life Sciences contracts in India. US pipeline "similar to same period 12 months ago."

"Vicon secured two large Entertainment orders totalling £2.7 million from customers in Eastern Europe and Japan"

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

Gross margin FY25: 64.7% (FY24: 66.5%), down 180bps — driven by Smart Manufacturing mix (lower margin than Motion Capture). Adjusted EBIT: £2.2m (FY24: £1.7m), +29%.

Adjusted EBIT by division: Motion Capture £2.3m (FY24 restated: £1.5m); Smart Manufacturing £1.6m (FY24: £0.0m breakeven). PLC unallocated: −£1.7m (FY24: +£0.3m — note prior year benefited from interest income being in unallocated, now restructured).

Finance income declining trajectory: FY23 £1.6m → FY24 £2.3m → FY25 £1.3m (or £1.7m cash received). Further decline expected in FY26 as cash depletes.

Cost discipline: annualised savings of ~£1.2m from FY24 restructure flowed through FY25. Operating cash generation before tax improved to £6.7m (FY24: £0.3m).

"operating cash inflows before tax improved to £6.7m (FY24: £0.3m), benefitting from a £4.9m improvement in working capital"

Gross margin headwind from Smart Manufacturing mix shift is structural and ongoing — as SM grows to a larger proportion of revenues, blended gross margin will continue to decline gradually.

5. Capital returns and per-share items

Dividend: FY25 final 3.25p (unchanged vs FY24 final 3.25p; FY24 prior year final was 2.75p). Proposed final dividend at AGM 25 Feb 2026. Cash impact ~£3.8m (113.1m shares × 3.25p). Dividend not covered by statutory EPS of −0.55p — explicitly noted by directors. Covered by adjusted EPS of 1.55p but only just (3.25p >> 1.55p). This is a clear capital allocation tension.

Share buyback: £8.3m deployed in FY25 buying 15.9m shares at avg £0.52. Programme extended to £10m total. As of Dec 2025, ~£8.6m deployed total. Shares in issue reduced from ~131m to ~115m (Sharescope shows 113.1m current).

Net cash: £37.3m year end FY25 (includes £22m FTDs + £15.3m cash). Down from £50.7m FY24.

"£12.5m returned to shareholders through buybacks and dividends"

6. Qualitative tone

AGM statement (25 Feb 2026) — the most recent forward-looking RNS: "solid trading momentum across both divisions", "encouraging operational progress". Key new data points: IVMS formation (Sempre + IVS merger from 1 March 2026), £2.7m Vicon entertainment orders confirmed, US motion capture "market conditions are largely unchanged." Strategy to be set out in H1 FY26.

"The Board remains confident in delivering further progress through FY26, supported by growing pipelines, planned Motion Capture product launches and the benefits of unifying the Smart Manufacturing division."

Markerless: "pipeline has continued to grow in value and customer interest remains strong" — still pre-revenue scale; "modest revenues" repeatedly the language used.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

The primary forward-looking RNS being scored is the FY25 Preliminary Results (Dec 2025) supplemented by the AGM Statement (25 Feb 2026) which is the most recent RNS in the package.

Assessing forward guidance for FY26 only:

The company guides to: (a) FY26 Adjusted EBIT "in line with Board's expectations" — qualitative only; (b) Q1 trading "in line with expectations"; (c) specific order wins at AGM (£2.7m entertainment); (d) IVMS formation; (e) US "unchanged" (not worsening); (f) strategy to be set out in H1 FY26; (g) 15-month FY26 year providing a structural revenue uplift.

Guidance type: qualitative, one year. No numeric uplift provided. The 15-month year provides a mechanical revenue tailwind that is visible to brokers but management is not explicitly calling it out as an "upgrade trigger."

The "in line with Board's expectations" language with a positive qualitative overlay (solid trading, growing pipelines, IVMS synergies, £2.7m orders) is constructive but falls short of explicit upgrade language. The dividend sustainability question and US headwind caveat are material constraints.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — "in line with Board's expectations" with positive operational overlays; 15-month year provides structural upside vs trailing 12-month models; IVMS formation a margin catalyst; no downgrade language. Provisional points: +6 to +8.

Divergence check: FY25 adjusted EBIT +29% (beat vs FY24), adjusted EPS −49% (miss vs FY24, driven entirely by finance income decline). The "beat" on EBIT is directionally positive for FY26 operational leverage. The "miss" on EPS vs FY24 reflects a structural change (lower cash → lower interest income) not an operational deterioration. Guidance is Constructive vs mixed EPS delivery — no strong divergence signal. Flagged as: ⚠️ EPS decline is structural (interest income depletion), not operational. Forward operational trajectory is improving. No beat-quality divergence required.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

OMG · Q4 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 30/09/25

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-check (Sharescope H2 field corruption check):

  • FY23 (2y ago): H1 £21.3m + H2 £23.0m = £44.3m. RNS states FY23 revenue £44.2m. Difference £0.1m — rounding. ✅ No corruption.
  • FY23 EPS: H1 2.9p + H2 2.4p = 5.3p. Sharescope shows FY 5.3p. ✅ Confirmed.
  • FY24 (1y ago): H1 £23.5m + H2 £17.9m = £41.4m. RNS states FY24 £41.5m. Difference £0.1m — rounding. ✅
  • FY24 EPS: H1 2.6p + H2 0.4p = 3.0p. Sharescope shows FY 3.0p. ✅ (Note: RNS shows FY24 adjusted basic EPS 3.01p — consistent with Sharescope 3.0p rounding.)
  • FY25 (current): H1 £20.1m + H2 £24.7m = £44.8m. RNS confirms £44.8m. ✅
  • FY25 EPS: H1 0.1p + H2 1.4p = 1.5p. RNS shows adjusted basic EPS 1.55p. ✅ Consistent (rounding).
  • FY22 (3y ago): H1 12.5 + H2 16.3 = £28.8m. No RNS FY22 figures in data package — treat as Sharescope-sourced.

No H2 field corruption detected across any period. All fields confirmed.

Both represent revenue decline and EPS increase vs FY25 on like-for-like basis. Flagged — not directly comparable.

Revenue growth trajectory: FY22→FY23: +53% (COVID recovery/pent-up demand surge). FY23→FY24: −6% (normalisation). FY24→FY25: +8% (Smart Manufacturing contribution). 🔴 Decelerating on the core Vicon business (−6% then +8% driven by inorganic); underlying Motion Capture revenue declining in each of last two years. The +8% headline masks a −17% Motion Capture decline offset by +341% Smart Manufacturing — structurally mixed.

EPS growth trajectory: FY23: +112% (peak). FY24: −43%. FY25: −48%. 🔴 Decelerating — three-year EPS trend is strongly negative. FY26e consensus +68% is the recovery forecast but on a 15-month year basis. Underlying EPS recovery is the core investment thesis but has not yet materialised.

Acceleration flags:

  • Revenue: FY26e YoY +10% (but 15-month distortion). FY25 actual YoY was +8% (RNS-derived). On like-for-like: FY26e 12m equivalent growth vs FY25 actual is ~−12%. No genuine revenue acceleration. Flag: no acceleration (consensus-distorted by 15-month year).
  • EPS: FY26e +68% vs FY25 −48%. On like-for-like 12m basis: FY26e 12m equivalent ~2.1p vs FY25 1.55p = +35%. Genuine EPS recovery inflecting upward. Flag: acceleration ✓ (consensus-derived, 12m-adjusted) — though starting from a depressed base.

EPS trajectory (last 3 HoH YoY figures): FY24 H2: −83%; FY25 H1: −95%; FY25 H2: +250%. 🟡 Volatile — extreme swings driven by comparison base effects (FY23/FY24 were abnormally high; FY25 H2 bounces off near-zero base). The +250% H2 FY25 is mechanically flattering (0.4p → 1.4p). Underlying adjusted EBIT is recovering gradually but EPS is heavily distorted by finance income movements.

Revenue trajectory (last 3 HoH YoY figures): FY24 H2: −22%; FY25 H1: −14%; FY25 H2: +38%. 🟡 Volatile — H2 FY25 recovery driven by Smart Manufacturing seasonal step-up (Sempre full contribution in H2). Not yet a clean trend.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Data source gate: H1 figures not yet published for FY26 (Q4 routing = post-FY results, next event is H1 FY26 results expected ~June 2026). No H1 actuals in any RNS provided. AGM statement (25 Feb 2026) provides qualitative colour only ("solid trading momentum"; specific order wins) — no H1 revenue or EPS figure disclosed. RNS conditions (1), (2), (3) all unmet. Both metrics: UNTRACKABLE.

Revenue baseline for FY26 H1:

  • 3yr avg H1% = 49.4% (from Sharescope). FY26e £49.1m × 49.4% = £24.3m H1 revenue baseline.
  • Buy trigger threshold: £24.3m × 1.015 = £24.6m
  • Sell trigger threshold: £24.3m × 0.985 = £23.9m

EPS baseline for FY26 H1:

  • 3yr avg H1% = 52.5% (from Sharescope). FY26e 2.6p × 52.5% = 1.37p H1 EPS baseline.
  • Buy trigger: 1.37p × 1.015 = 1.39p
  • Sell trigger: 1.37p × 0.985 = 1.35p

⚠️ Critical caveat: FY26 is a 15-month year ending 31 Dec 2026. The "H1" period will be six months (Oct 2025 – Mar 2026). The £49.1m consensus is for 15 months. Applying a 49.4% H1 split to £49.1m will significantly overstate the expected H1 contribution — the 15-month year is back-end weighted (it includes a full Oct–Dec quarter which is historically strong for OMG). The genuine H1 (Oct–Mar) baseline should be derived against a 12-month FY26e run-rate of ~£39.3m: £39.3m × 49.4% = £19.4m as the better H1 revenue reference point. Both thresholds stated above for reference; use with caution.

Signal: UNTRACKABLE (no H1 actuals disclosed). H1 results expected ~June 2026. Note to confirm at that date.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-H1 mode — compare implied H2 vs avg of last 3 historical H2s)

H2 base figure: No updated FY26 guidance in RNS — using FY26e consensus £49.1m revenue and 2.6p EPS. FY26 H1 actual unknown. Using FY25 H1 actual as H1 proxy would be methodologically incorrect for FY26 H2 derivation. In pre-H1 mode, Phase 3.3 assesses whether the implied FY26 H2 required by consensus is plausible given historical H2 patterns.

Derivation: Implied FY26 H2 = FY26e fc − FY26 H1 baseline (3yr avg)

  • Revenue: £49.1m − £24.3m (H1 baseline) = £24.8m implied H2
  • EPS: 2.6p − 1.37p (H1 baseline) = 1.23p implied H2

vs historical H2 actuals (last 3): Revenue: FY23 H2 £23.0m / FY24 H2 £17.9m / FY25 H2 £24.7m. Avg: £21.9m.

  • Implied FY26 H2 £24.8m vs avg £21.9m → +13% above avg. Classification: 🟢 moderate/strong. Achievable — FY25 H2 was already £24.7m so consensus H2 is essentially flat YoY for H2 on 12-month equivalent.

⚠️ 15-month year distortion: However, the 15-month FY26 includes the Q1 (Oct–Dec 2025) and Q2 (Jan–Mar 2026) which together form "H1", then Q3 (Apr–Jun 2026) and Q4 (Jul–Sep 2026) form "H2", with a further Q5 period (Oct–Dec 2026) forming the extra quarter. The implied H2 calculation above is mechanically distorted by the non-standard year. On a clean 12-month FY26 run-rate of ~£39.3m, the H2 burden would be £39.3m − £19.4m = £19.9m — below recent H2 actuals. This would classify as 🟡 flat/moderate — achievable.

EPS H2: implied 1.23p vs avg of last 3 H2s (2.4p, 0.4p, 1.4p) = avg 1.43p. Implied H2 1.23p is −14% below avg — 🟡 flat/weak on 12-month equivalent. The EPS H2 burden is manageable given the FY25 H2 was 1.4p — consensus is essentially calling for H2 FY26 (12m basis) EPS similar to FY25 H2, with H1 recovering strongly to 1.37p vs FY25 H1 0.12p. The H1 recovery is where the bull case lives.

Profit warning feasibility gate: Not triggered — H1 tracking is UNTRACKABLE (no miss confirmed), operating leverage is not elevated (net cash), no fixed cost headwinds flagged by management.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change over full snapshot period (May 2025 to Apr 2026): 2.7p → 2.6p, net −0.1p (−3.7%). One downgrade step: Jun 2025 (2.7p → 2.6p) and second in Feb 2026 (back to 2.6p after no change). Upgrades vs downgrades: 0 upgrades, 2 downgrade steps in the period. No upgrades observed.
  • Revenue trend: Net change: 46.6m → 49.1m, +£2.5m (+5.4%). Major upward step in Dec 2025 (£44.8m → £49.1m) — this reflects the 15-month year recalibration by brokers following the accounting reference date change announcement. Not organic EPS/EBIT upgrades.
  • 4-week EPS trend: 🟡 FLAT — 2.6p held throughout last 4 weeks.
  • Divergence: Price has declined from 100p (May 2025) to 44.85p (current) — a 55% decline over ~11 months. EPS consensus has barely moved (−3.7%). This is a significant price/consensus divergence — the market is clearly sceptical of the consensus or applying a structural re-rating downward (post-derating of small-cap tech, AIM liquidity concerns, dividend sustainability questions).
